official.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS) is for excellent students joining a full-time Leiden University Master's degree programme, with the exception of LLM (non-advanced) and MSc programmes at Leiden Law School. It is awarded for the duration of the study programme at one of five tuition-fee levels, and Leiden states it is not a full scholarship, so a significant personal contribution will be required.
official.program_type: Study scholarship for incoming non-EEA/non-EFTA master's students

applicant_utility.summary: The LExS pays a fixed slice of Leiden's non-EEA tuition bill - between EUR 10,000 and EUR 19,000 depending on your programme's fee level - and nothing toward rent, insurance or flights, so you must be able to fund the rest before you apply. The scholarship is not a separate form: you submit the master's admission application first, then open the Scholarships section inside it and attach a 500-word motivation PDF. With only about 25 awards against more than a thousand applicants, treat it as a reach award that sits on top of other funding, never as your financial plan.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-decile graduates from outside the EEA/EFTA applying to an eligible September-start Leiden master's who can already show the remaining tuition plus living and visa funds.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and submit the admission application well before 1 December 2026 - Leiden warns it can take up to 3 working days before the Scholarships section appears
Check which of the five published tuition-fee levels applies to your programme so you know your realistic remaining bill
Draft the motivation letter as a PDF of maximum 500 words explaining why you should be considered for the award
Prepare one complete LExS application plus motivation letter inside every separate admission application if you apply for more than one programme or specialisation
Confirm you hold no other full scholarship from an external provider, and line up proof of sufficient funds for the Dutch residence permit
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 December deadline - late scholarship applications are explicitly not considered
The LExS never appearing in the Scholarships section because the admission application was not submitted, was late, or the programme is excluded (e.g. non-advanced LLM or MSc at Leiden Law School)
Applying while eligible for Dutch student finance (Studiefinanciering) or already holding a Leiden University master's degree
Submitting a motivation letter over 500 words or in the wrong file format, then trying to email corrections after submission, which is not possible
For UK applicants: having been registered in the Dutch BRP before 1 January 2021, which removes eligibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the tuition-fee level awarded: the remaining tuition, all living costs, health insurance and travel, plus the proof of sufficient funds non-EEA recipients must show for the residence permit.
document_audit: The motivation letter must be a single PDF of maximum 500 words - word count and format are hard constraints
Nothing may be added or changed after submission, either online or by email
Recipients must confirm agreement with the LExS terms and conditions in writing before the award is finalised
alerts: The 1 December 2026 deadline applies to the scholarship section inside the admission application - a late admission application silently kills the scholarship bid
February-start programmes are excluded, as are Leiden Law School's non-advanced LLM and MSc programmes
The award level is final and non-negotiable once granted, and the LExS cannot be stacked with another full external scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online admission application, reopen the Apply screen, tick the LExS in the Scholarships section, upload the 500-word PDF and submit - faculty committees then nominate within 10 weeks and all applicants hear before the end of March.

applicant_utility.summary: The NL Scholarship is a single EUR 5,000 payment landing in your first year at Groningen, and the university says outright that it does not cover your living and study costs - so budget as though it will not arrive and treat it as a bonus if it does. You can only apply once you already hold an admission offer for a programme on the published list, and the file must be complete, since incomplete applications are not considered at all. Because it can be received only once in a lifetime, spend the application on the programme you genuinely most want to attend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA bachelor's graduates with no prior Dutch education who already hold a Groningen admission offer for a listed master's and can show a strong transcript plus a clear, Netherlands-linked plan.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target master's actually appears on the applicable-programmes list before building any plans around the award
Secure the Groningen admission offer first - it is the gate to even opening the application form
Prepare a transcript covering all undergraduate courses so far, not just final results
Write the motivation letter to explicitly tie studying in the Netherlands to your future academic and professional goals, which is what the committee scores
Assemble all three documents in one complete submission before the deadline; a missing item voids the file
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete application - the university states incomplete applications will not be taken into consideration

Any prior Dutch diploma or previous education in the Netherlands (exchanges excepted) removing eligibility

A motivation letter that never connects the Groningen programme to future goals, which the selection procedure explicitly weighs
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Non-EEA tuition fees for the whole programme, almost all living costs, health insurance and travel - the EUR 5,000 is a one-year living contribution only.
document_audit: The transcript must cover all undergraduate courses so far, including incomplete years
